reasoning_trace.value: The paper includes several figures and tables that provide visual details about the proposed traveling wave antenna-on-display (TWAoD) for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) applications. Figure 1 illustrates the concept of a single-platform TWAoD array within a mobile terminal for 2-dimensional frequency scanning and phase scanning modes. Figure 2 presents the proposed TWAoD ISAC antenna structure utilizing FS/PS modes for different scenarios. Figure 3 shows the frequency scanning (FS) mode at the xoz-plane and phase scanning (PS) mode at the yoz-plane. Figure 4 displays the configuration of the proposed TWAoD unit cell in the display region and its simulated dispersion diagram. Figure 5 illustrates the design scheme of the proposed TWAoD unit cell. Figure 6 presents the current vector diagram and electric-field distribution of the proposed unit cell. Figure 7 shows the 3-D view of a single radiating element and its simulated radiation patterns. Figure 8 presents the configuration of the 1×8 TWAoD array with passive and active feeding types. Figure 9 displays the simulated radiation patterns of the proposed 2-D beam steering antenna at different frequencies and phase shifts. Figure 10 shows the simulated and measured S-parameter and peak realized gain of the proposed 1×8 TWAoD array. Figure 11 presents the simulated and measured beam steering patterns for FS and PS modes. Figure 12 illustrates the configuration of the proposed FPC-based diplexer for ISAC applications and its simulated and measured S-parameters. Figure 13 shows the photograph of the fabricated TWAoD array with a diplexer for ISAC systems and its configuration. Figure 14 displays the configuration of the proposed ISAC TWAoD array with an FPC-based ISAC active feed network and its simulated and measured H-/E-plane radiation patterns. Figure 15 presents the proposed test setup for evaluating the ISAC system's radar and communication performance.

reasoning_trace.value: The proposed TWAoD features a traveling wave antenna integrated into the transparent region of the display panel, enabling simultaneous 2-D phase and frequency beam scanning for ISAC applications. The TWAoD utilizes a grid-shaped with cross-over patch structure, allowing for EH1-mode radiation and enabling 2-D beam scanning through frequency-dependent angle variation and phased array principles.

reasoning_trace.value: The paper reports experimental results showing that the TWAoD achieves high gain and dual-mode capability for radar and communication at 24 and 28 GHz, respectively. The measured impedance bandwidth ascertains |S11| < -10dB across 20-40 GHz, and the peak gain is achieved in the range of 10-12 dBi (simulated)/9.8-11.3 dBi (measured) across the operating bands (22-38GHz). The measured H-plane scanning angle is set as -52° to +47° in the 22–37 GHz, and the E-plane phase beam scanning pattern achieves approximately ±58° at 28 GHz.
